children.text: Video Games have evolved to include very complex world building and story lines. Advancements in technology have allowed this, because they've enabled more detailed game mechanics, and allowed for the construction of games that require more processing speed, and memory capacity.

Games like Baldur's Gate III have multiple maps, dozens of quest lines, and multiple characters will fully fleshed out storylines. They allow you to have relationships with in-game characters, with good and bad dialogue options that can completely change the outcome of the storyline. The game play is structured like Dungeons and Dragons, so choices have levels of difficulty, and you must roll a dice to determine the outcome of a situation. It is designed to be pass fail, but there are ways you can save your progress and ensure you have the option of making a better decision.

, are multiplayer games, where it requires the coordinated efforts of two players to navigate the complex map, and work as a team to pass each level. The game play is designed to be entirely interactive, and you must have a second person to play the game with you, or it will be impossible.

, two authors are given a chance to publish their books by a company, if they participate in an experiment first. The intention of the experiment is to harvest their ideas, so the authors must play through every story world they've ever thought of, in order to protect their ideas from being exploited. The complex narrative design of the game speaks to the theft of artwork by AI, and the uselessness of copyright laws to protect stolen work.

Gaming narrative speaks to very complex morality issues, and is able to explore detailed themes, in a similar manner to movies or books. The choice-based games also encourage the reader to look at their own morality, and to question whether they are making the right decision with each step of the way.

title: The Evolution of Narratives within Video Games
